_doc: THE LAYERS TYPE FILTER, as one shared truth for both active ports.
Each vector is a flattened tree given as (path, type) rows plus the set of
hidden type tokens, and the paths that must survive. Both ports run these
through the same function -- jas_dioxus `tree_type_filter_keep`, JasSwift
`layersTypeFilterKeep` -- so the algorithm has ONE definition rather than
two hand-written test suites that agree today and drift later.
WHY THIS FAMILY EXISTS. `layers_hidden_types` is VIEW STATE, and
transcripts/CORPUS_CENSUS.md flagged view state as the corpus's thinnest
coverage: almost every fixture runs at the identity view, where nothing that
depends on view state can fail. The only prior exception was
test_fixtures/actions/view_state.json (zoom / offset).
AND WHY IT EXISTS *NOW*. On 2026-07-29 jas_dioxus was found deriving each
row's type by PARSING ITS DISPLAY LABEL -- matching `<Rectangle>` apart and
letting anything else fall to `""` -- so an element the artist had NAMED was
exempt from the filter. Correct the day it was written (only Layers could be
named), silently wrong from the commit that let every element carry a name.
JasSwift had always matched on the element, so the two ports disagreed for
months in the panel an artist reads most, and NO fixture anywhere could see
it: the filter lived in private per-port view code.
THE ROWS CARRY TYPES, NOT LABELS, DELIBERATELY. A vector that spelled its
rows as display names would re-enact the defect inside the very corpus meant
to prevent it. `name` is present on some rows only to prove it is IGNORED.
EVERY VECTOR ALSO DECLARES `expected_ancestor_only` -- the paths that survive
ONLY because a descendant needs them. It is DERIVED (keep \\ visible), not
hand-written, so it cannot drift from the keep-set it describes; both readers
recompute it and compare.
It exists because those rows are a different KIND of row, which the ruling
makes explicit: scaffolding is CARRIED, NEVER MATCHED, and renders dimmed.
Adding the channel also un-vacuums a vector that had been asserting nothing:
`every_leaf_hidden_layer_survives_on_its_own_type` was written to distinguish
'survived on its own type' from 'survived as an ancestor', and with only
`expected_keep` to look at, BOTH readings produced [[0]] -- so the vector
could not fail either way. Starbuck found that at arbitration; it is closed
here.
VECTORS MARKED `ruled: R1/2026-07-30` CARRY A COUNCIL RULING, no longer a
question. JYH ruled the filter in CHECKED-SEMANTICS: a checked type lists all
its elements, PLUS THEIR ANCESTORS; nothing checked (the default) means
everything. Stated that way the ancestor rule stops being an awkward
exception and becomes half the definition -- and the old spec sentence
("unchecking a type hides all elements of that type"), which was simply FALSE
for containers, dies with it.
The keep-sets below did not move, and that is the point: checked and
unchecked are complements over the menu, so the shipping algorithm was always
computing the ruled rule. The implementation was never wrong. THE SENTENCE
WAS. What the ruling adds is a reason for a row to be present -- it matched,
or an ancestor obligation carried it -- and those two are different kinds of
row, which is what the pending dimming work renders.
TWO AXES, NEVER DERIVED FROM EACH OTHER (the same council). Search is the
NAME axis and matches the displayed label as literal text -- `ath` finds
`<Path>` and `math` alike, across all types. The filter is the TYPE axis and
reads the element. The auto-generated `<Circle>` label is NOT a type
indicator; it is just a name. See the last two vectors: a circle the artist
named `<Rectangle>` is still a circle.

vectors.name: named_leaf_is_filtered
vectors.doc: THE DEFECT. Two rectangles, one named 'roof', beside a circle. Hiding `rectangle` must remove BOTH. jas_dioxus kept the named one because its label was 'roof' rather than '<Rectangle>'.

vectors.name: a_name_is_not_a_type
vectors.doc: Every row named, none unnamed. Under the old label parse EVERY hint came out empty and the filter was a total no-op -- the worst case, and the one an artist who names their work would hit every time.

vectors.name: empty_name_is_not_a_name
vectors.doc: An empty string is not a name -- it falls back to the bracket label in `elementDisplayName` / `tree_elem_display_name`. It must not perturb the TYPE either way.

vectors.name: nothing_hidden_keeps_everything
vectors.doc: The identity case. Both ports guard on a non-empty hidden set before calling, so production never passes this -- pinned anyway, because a function whose identity case is undefined is a function whose guard is load-bearing and unstated.

vectors.name: hidden_type_nothing_has
vectors.doc: Hiding `text` in a document with no Text element removes nothing. Guards against a filter that drops rows it cannot classify -- which is exactly what the label parse did to named rows, in reverse.

vectors.name: every_leaf_hidden_layer_survives_on_its_own_type
vectors.doc: Both leaves hidden. The layer survives because ITS OWN type is not hidden -- NOT because it is an ancestor, since nothing under it survives. The two reasons a container can be kept are distinguished here on purpose; a filter that conflated them would pass the ancestor vectors below by accident.

vectors.name: container_kept_as_ancestor_of_a_survivor
vectors.doc: Hiding `group` does NOT remove the group, because its rectangle survives and a tree cannot draw a child without its parent row. So unchecking Group is very nearly a no-op today, while layers.yaml says it 'hides all elements of that type'. Identical in both ports.

vectors.name: container_removed_when_its_whole_subtree_is_hidden
vectors.doc: The other half of the same rule, and what makes it a REACHABILITY rule rather than an exemption: hide the container AND its only descendant type, and the container does disappear.

vectors.name: ancestor_chain_two_levels_deep
vectors.doc: The keep-set walks EVERY proper prefix, not just the immediate parent. A one-level implementation would drop the middle group and orphan the survivor.

vectors.name: sibling_containers_resolve_independently
vectors.doc: Two groups under one layer: one holds a survivor, one does not. The first is kept as an ancestor, the second removed. A keep-set computed per-container rather than per-surviving-row would keep both.

vectors.name: sibling_index_is_compared_elementwise
vectors.doc: Paths are prefixes ELEMENT-WISE, never as joined strings: [0,1] is not an ancestor of [0,10]. A string-prefix implementation would keep [0,1] as an ancestor of the surviving [0,10] and the wrong row would stay on screen. Same hazard `check_selection_invariant.py` guards for selections.

vectors.name: the_filter_is_uniform_over_tokens_the_menu_restricts
vectors.doc: A live element answers `live`. The FUNCTION honours that token like any other -- this vector proves it, by feeding it in and expecting the row gone. What no live element can be hidden BY is the menu, whose eleven `lp_filter_button` items do not include it, so `live` cannot reach the hidden set in production. Keeping the restriction in the MENU rather than as a special case in the filter is what makes this a declared shared gap (UNOFFERABLE in scripts/check_layers_type_filter.py) instead of a divergence: the day the menu gains the option, both ports already work. If a port ever special-cased live elements here, this vector moves.

vectors.name: a_circle_named_rectangle_is_still_a_circle
vectors.doc: THE RULING IN ITS STRONGEST FORM (JYH, 2026-07-30): the auto-generated label `<Path>` / `<Circle>` is NOT an indicator of type -- it is just a name, and rename accepts any string, brackets included. So an artist can name a circle '<Rectangle>', and it is STILL A CIRCLE: hidden when Circle is hidden, untouched when Rectangle is. Search, by contrast, treats the same label as literal text ('ath' matches '<Path>' and 'math' alike). Two axes -- name and type -- and neither may be derived from the other.

vectors.name: and_hiding_circle_takes_it_despite_its_name
vectors.doc: The other half of the same ruling: hide Circle and the '<Rectangle>'-named circle goes, its real rectangle sibling stays. Together with the vector above, these two pin that the filter is a pure function of the type channel -- the name channel cannot save an element from its type nor condemn it to another's.
